mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 3% annualized rate, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input constraints and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, exceeding 0.5 percentage points over 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises significantly (Conference Board index up > 5 points) in the quarter following the unemployment rate spike, indicating the labor market weakness is transient.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, indicating the market is not responding to the restrictive policy signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts rise by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 30-year mortgage rates rise by > 100 basis points in the 3 months following the housing starts spike, indicating the housing strength is likely to be short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth < -100k jobs/mo for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall significantly (< 10% from peak) in the month following the payroll growth slowdown, indicating the labor market weakness is likely temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales growth accelerates by more than 5% year-over-year, it signals a surge in consumer spending that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer sentiment plunges (> 10 point drop) in the month following the retail sales surge, indicating the spending strength is likely to be short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a potential inflation scare that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in a more aggressive Fed response.
failure_condition: Breakeven inflation expectations (10y-10y) rise significantly (> 20 basis points) in the week following the inflation scare signal, indicating the market expects the Fed to successfully contain inflation without aggressive rate hikes.
